key_insight: A three-dimensional collision-region model predicts substantial angular variation in energy dissipation for equal impinging liquid jets, even with uniform inlet and sheet mean velocities.
engineering_relevance: Angularly resolved dissipation estimates could guide impinging-jet mixer design where local mixing intensity matters.
method: Model collision-region thickness as varying linearly from the stagnation point to the outer boundary along each radial line.
Combine modeled volume with collision-induced kinetic energy loss to estimate mass-specific dissipation.
Calculate overall and narrow-angular-sector-averaged dissipation rates.
evidence_signal: The model recovers expected theoretical limits, including a cylindrical region for directly opposed jets, and preliminary micromixing results are consistent with its predicted angular variation.
watch_item: The assumed collision-region geometry and the location of energy dissipation still require independent validation.
paper_title: Azimuthally Resolved Energy Dissipation Rates in the Impingement Zone of Equal Free Impinging Liquid Jets: A Three-Dimensional Model
